description: How much credit support and revenue-share exposure will NVIDIA have extended to AI cloud partners under its new AI-factory business model, and what contingent liability does that represent?
outcome: The amount of credit support/guarantees and revenue-share commitments NVIDIA discloses, and whether the exposure is material to its cash and credit risk.
period: NVIDIA's next annual report (Form 10-K) after the July 2026 announcement

description: Will NVIDIA's Vera Rubin AI chip platform reach revenue-generating first shipments by the end of calendar 2026?
outcome: Whether Vera Rubin begins shipping in 2026, as the item reports it 'could begin shipping later this year'.
period: End of calendar 2026 — the item states Vera Rubin is in full production and 'could begin shipping later this year' (2026); check date set at year-end 2026.

description: Will NVIDIA's U.S.-approved H200 chip sales to China translate into revenue-generating shipments by NVIDIA's fiscal year-end January 2027?
outcome: Whether Chinese authorities permit H200 sales to Chinese commercial customers and NVIDIA records China data-center revenue from those shipments by the check date.
period: NVIDIA's fiscal year-end (late January 2027), set as the current fiscal year-end for a pending regulatory decision.

description: How much will the big four AI hyperscalers spend on data-center capital expenditures in calendar 2026, and does the aggregate reach the ~$650 billion currently planned?
outcome: The combined 2026 data-center capex the four largest AI hyperscalers actually report/spend, versus the ~$650 billion currently planned and NVIDIA's ~$1 trillion projection for the following year.
period: Calendar year 2026 — checked against the hyperscalers' reported full-year 2026 capex in their Q4 2026 earnings releases (early 2027).

description: Will NVIDIA's Kyber NVL144 rack-scale architecture, designed to house its 2027 Rubin Ultra chips, reach revenue-generating first shipments in calendar 2027 as originally planned, or slip to 2028 as SemiAnalysis reports?
outcome: Whether the Kyber rack debuts and ships with Vera Rubin Ultra in calendar 2027 (consistent with NVIDIA's 'roadmap is intact') or is delayed to 2028 (SemiAnalysis), and when first shipments actually occur.
period: Calendar 2027 first shipments — the item says Kyber 'had been slated to debut with Vera Rubin Ultra ... in 2027' and reports a >12-month delay to 2028; whether 2027 shipments occur can be checked at year-end 2027, with 2028 as the reported slip date.

description: How much will DRAM, NAND and high-bandwidth memory contract prices rise in calendar 2026, and what will the memory content of NVIDIA's Vera Rubin VR200 rack cost, now that memory is reported to be 25-30% of the rack bill of materials?
outcome: The direction and size of 2026 memory contract price increases and the memory cost per NVIDIA Vera Rubin rack (Morgan Stanley currently puts memory content at about $2 million per rack, up 435%), which bears on NVIDIA's per-rack cost/ASP economics and on hyperscaler AI-infrastructure spending.
period: Calendar year 2026 — checked against memory contract price releases and NVIDIA/partner disclosures of rack bill-of-materials as Vera Rubin ramps during H2 2026.

description: What will NVIDIA's outstanding supply (purchase) commitments to its manufacturing and memory suppliers total at its next annual report?
outcome: The supply-commitments balance NVIDIA discloses in its next Form 10-K, versus the $119 billion reported in this item, and whether the obligation is growing faster than the revenue it supports (which would raise write-down or utilisation risk if hyperscaler orders slow).
period: NVIDIA's next annual report (Form 10-K, fiscal year ending late January 2027) — the next annual report for an obligation already undertaken, as section 3 fixes for such obligations.

description: Will the spot rental price of an NVIDIA H100 GPU-hour keep falling through calendar 2026, dropping below the ~$3.20/hour peak reached in May 2026, as custom accelerators and easing GPU supply pressure the market price of compute?
outcome: The trajectory of H100 GPU-hour spot rental prices (Ornn compute-marketplace index) over calendar 2026 — whether the rate continues to decline from the ~$3.20/hour May 2026 peak.
period: Calendar year 2026 — checked against Ornn's published H100 spot rental-price index at year-end 2026.

description: Will the French competition authority conclude its antitrust investigation into NVIDIA's cloud-AI and GPU practices and impose remedies or fines, and by when?
outcome: Whether the French competition authority issues a decision (behavioral remedies, commitments or fines) closing its probe into alleged anti-competitive practices in NVIDIA's cloud-AI and GPU markets.
period: NVIDIA's current fiscal year-end (late January 2027) — set as the check date for a pending regulatory decision the item dates only as 'nearing a conclusion'.

description: How much will the top U.S. hyperscalers spend on custom AI accelerators (ASIC/XPU chips such as those Marvell designs for Amazon and Microsoft) in calendar 2026, and how much AI-accelerator demand is bypassing NVIDIA GPUs?
outcome: The dollar volume of hyperscaler custom-ASIC purchases in calendar 2026 (as reflected in the ASIC vendors' custom AI silicon revenue) versus those hyperscalers' NVIDIA GPU purchases — a measure of how far AI compute is shifting from NVIDIA GPUs to custom silicon for inference.
period: Calendar year 2026 (this calendar year relative to the 14 July 2026 item), checked against ASIC vendors' and hyperscalers' calendar-2026 disclosures in early 2027.
